target.title: fix(browser): finalize assistant turns on positive completion proof (stop preamble/mid-stream capture)
target.body:
## Problem

Long-running ChatGPT Pro browser turns can stream an opening preamble, briefly settle, then continue through reasoning/tool work before producing the real answer. Oracle could treat that first stable preamble as final because the old completion path inferred completion from quiet text and missing stop controls.

## Final design

This branch fails closed unless the sampled response has correlated positive terminal evidence:

- A finished-action bar must belong to the sampled message/turn, or to fallback markdown scoped under those controls and correlated after the current user turn.
- The action bar must remain present for a debounced number of cycles while the response fingerprint is unchanged for the minimum stability interval.
- Any content rewrite, including equal-length or shorter replacements, resets the debounce.
- Stop controls and strong live activity (shimmer, scoped `aria-busy`, verified thinking status, or scoped progress) veto completion.
- Text-only sidecar heuristics are weak evidence: they cannot override strong activity, but cannot hang a positively completed response.
- Elapsed quiet is never terminal proof. Selector drift or uncorrelated wrapperless layouts time out instead of returning a stable preamble or stale answer.
- Recovery, observer, and exhausted-budget paths all route through the same terminal-only poller and refuse unconfirmed text.

## Maintainer hardening

Rebased onto current `main`, including the hidden-window send fix from #302, and hardened through repeated AutoReview findings:

- separated strong live activity from weak or stale sidecar evidence;
- scoped progress, shimmer, and busy indicators to the current response or verified reasoning chrome;
- restricted status-label matching to verified thinking/reasoning UI;
- anchored completed-reasoning summaries, including heading-prefixed, worded-duration, concatenated, and trailing `Edit` variants;
- bound completion controls to the sampled message/turn and rejected stale earlier-turn controls;
- correlated wrapperless fallback candidates by DOM order after the current user turn;
- removed the absence-based quiet fallback entirely.

Maintainer commits are layered after the contributor's six original commits; contributor authorship and history remain intact.

## Validation

Exact final candidate head: `57d4a7afbac764dfd51f234811a2f1b6d3f3d38b`.

- `pnpm vitest run tests/browser/assistantResponseStatus.test.ts tests/browser/pageActions.test.ts tests/browser/index.test.ts tests/browser/promptComposer.test.ts tests/browser/chromeLifecycle.test.ts` — 214 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm check` — passed.
- `pnpm test` — 1,485 passed, 43 skipped.
- Final AutoReview: Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh — clean, no actionable findings.
- Public model identifier audit: PASS. GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6 are current public product names documented by OpenAI: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11909943-gpt-5-2-in-chatgpt and https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001354-gpt-56-in-chatgpt.

## Exact-head live Pro proof

Session `pr301-final-completion-live`, signed-in ChatGPT Pro, `--copy-profile`, `--browser-hide-window`, model selection verified as Pro:

- Initial turn captured all 30 requested numbered lines and the unique final marker `PR301-INITIAL-END-20260711`.
- Same-conversation follow-up captured all 20 requested numbered lines and the unique final marker `PR301-FOLLOWUP-END-20260711`.
- Both completed in 21.2 seconds total with no preamble-only or mid-stream truncation.

The contributor's original pre-hardening live proof also completed three real GPT-5.5 Pro runs in 701–1,270 seconds with zero retries and complete multi-kilobyte final reviews.

## Risk and behavior under drift

Risk remains medium/high because this is the central browser completion boundary. The final design deliberately chooses availability failure over silent truncation: if Oracle cannot correlate positive completion evidence, it times out and preserves recovery diagnostics instead of returning an incomplete or stale answer.

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`. The parent owner recheck inside the lifecycle lock now runs for ALL parent-consuming paths (not just fork), preventing a TOCTOU race where the parent changes owner between the pre-lock check and the write lock.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param + TOCTOU race fix for all paths), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (persist `pluginOwnerId` on reset), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings: ownerless parent protection, non-fork parent-session authorization, and TOCTOU race on non-fork and reset-main parent-consuming paths.

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  2 passed | 54 skipped (56) — 7 scenarios across 2 Vitest configs
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

**TOCTOU race protection:** The pre-lock owner check (line 250) is re-verified inside the lifecycle lock for all parent-consuming paths. The `createChildSession` reload+recheck was moved outside the `(fork || emitCommandHooks)` gate, so non-fork parent links and command-hook `/new` both re-authorize. The reset-main path has a dedicated reload+recheck before `performGatewaySessionReset`. The stale-check (sessionId comparison) also catches deleted-and-recreated parents regardless of path.

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **Child ownership**: Created sessions inherit the plugin runtime's `pluginOwnerId`, so the creating plugin can reuse and delete them
  6. **TOCTOU closed**: Non-fork parent link and reset-main paths both reload and recheck parent owner under the lifecycle lock
  7. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`)
- **Existing-target takeover**: Rejected (scenario 12) — Plugin B cannot take over Plugin A's session via explicit key
- **New-target create**: Allowed (scenario 13) — Plugin B creates at non-existent key, ownership stamped

**Live gateway RPC output (all 7 scenarios):**

| # | Scenario | Result | Response |
|---|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 2 | Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 3 | Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 4 | Plugin B non-fork parent → Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 5 | Plugin B non-fork parent → ownerless session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |

Environment: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22, commit `c85a663d556`

**Child ownership persistence:**

| # | Scenario | `entry.pluginOwnerId` |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent (child) | `undefined` ✅ (ownerless) |
| 10 | Plugin B fork from own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 11 | Plugin B parentless create (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |

- **Child reuse** (Scenario 8): Plugin B can use its own child as parent — allowed
- **Cross-plugin child denial** (Scenario 9): Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child — `INVALID_REQUEST`

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

Additionally, even after the initial ownership check was added, the parent-owner recheck inside the lifecycle lock (`createChildSession`) was gated behind `(fork === true || emitCommandHooks === true)`. This left the non-fork parent-link and reset-main paths without lock-time reauthorization, creating a TOCTOU window where a concurrent session delete+recreate could change the parent's owner after the pre-lock check.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. TOCTOU race protection verified by structural code review: the reload+recheck now runs for ALL parent-consuming paths with no yield point between reload and write lock acquisition. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Live gateway RPC proof — 10-scenario response table and child ownership persistence in Evidence section above
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Plugin B forking Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B forking ownerless session (rejected), non-plugin client forking any session (allowed), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to ownerless session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to own session (allowed), Plugin B child has `pluginOwnerId` persisted, Plugin B can reuse its child, Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child, Plugin B fork child has `pluginOwnerId`, Plugin B parentless create has `pluginOwnerId`
- Edge cases checked: no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` (skip check), ownerless parent (reject for plugins), self-ownership (allow), `fork === false` with `parentSessionKey` (now gated), child `pluginOwnerId` persistence (fork, non-fork, and parentless), TOCTOU race protection (reload+recheck for all paths)
- What you did NOT verify: Cross-store fork with `targetStorePath`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper review findings (ownerless protection + non-fork authorization).
- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper P1 TOCTOU race finding: moved reload+owner recheck outside `(fork || emitCommandHooks)` gate, added dedicated recheck in reset-main path.
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds new restrictions for cross-plugin and ownerless parent use; existing self-owned and non-plugin flows unchanged. This matches existing `sessions.delete` behavior.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the ownership check is placed in `createGatewaySession` at the service layer, close to where the parent session entry is resolved, rather than in the handler. This prevents future callers from accidentally bypassing the check. The unified check (fork + non-fork) mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` in delete — same rule, same surface. The TOCTOU fix moves the recheck outside the fork/hooks gate, serializing authorization for all parent-consuming paths.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the check is a self-contained change; `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` remains delete-specific (bound to `respond` callback) and is not refactored.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding the check in the `sessions.create` handler (sessions.ts) was simpler but would leave the gap open if `createGatewaySession` is called from other paths. Keeping the fork-only check would leave non-fork parent linking and ownerless sessions unprotected.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Prompt context included issue body, source-level provenance analysis of `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` and `createGatewaySession`, and ClawSweeper review discussion.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Low risk — this is an additive security hardening that narrows existing behavior. The check mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` which has been shipping since the delete path. Key mitigations:
- Non-plugin clients (the majority of callers) are entirely unaffected
- Plugin runtimes using their own sessions continue to work
- Ownerless session protection is consistent with existing delete behavior — plugins already cannot delete user sessions
- The TOCTOU race window is closed: the reload+recheck runs for all parent-consuming paths, and there is no yield point between the reload and the write lock acquisition
- The error message follows the same pattern as `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`

**Specific change from earlier PR revision**: The guard was expanded from fork-only to all parent-session use, and ownerless sessions are now protected. The TOCTOU race was fixed by moving the reload+owner recheck outside the `(fork || emitCommandHooks)` gate.

---

Related to #103089

**Environment:** Linux 4.19.112, Node v22.19.0, commit \`5bc7ae852b4\`

2. **Reset-main path**: added dedicated `loadSessionEntry` + owner recheck before `performGatewaySessionReset`

4. **Active-work check**: remains nested inside `(emitCommandHooks || fork)` — only relevant for those paths


target.body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of #46217: replaces 20 hardcoded English strings in the Settings view toolbar with `t()` calls under a new `settings.*` namespace in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`. Runs `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` to regenerate all 18 locale bundles. `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` ship with native-speaker translations (seeded into the TM so they survive future sync runs); other locales fall through to English fallback per the existing no-provider behavior.

Strings covered (toolbar chrome only):
- Mode toggle: `Form`, `Raw`, plus the two toggle tooltips and `Raw mode unavailable for this snapshot`
- Changes badge: `Unsaved changes` (raw mode), `{count} unsaved change` / `{count} unsaved changes` (form mode, sing/plural — fix applied after @clawsweeper review), `No changes`
- Action buttons: `Open`, `Open config file`, `Open {path}` tooltip, `Clear`, `Apply` / `Applying…`, `Update` / `Updating…`
- Search: placeholder, aria-label, clear-search aria-label
- Accordion: `Quick Settings` header
- `Raw mode disabled (snapshot cannot safely round-trip raw text).` notice

The `Save` / `Saving…` button reuses existing `common.save` / `common.saving` keys (which already carry native translations across all locales — `保存` / `保存中…` in zh-CN, `儲存` / `儲存中…` in zh-TW). The sing/plural pair `unsavedChangeCount` / `unsavedChangesCount` follows the repo's existing pattern (`common.checkpoint` / `common.checkpoints`).

## Out of scope (separate PRs to follow)

Per the @clawsweeper review on #46217, the full localization touches three additional surfaces that intentionally are NOT in this PR:

- `SECTION_CATEGORIES` and `SECTION_META` (category and section labels like "Core", "AI & Agents") — defer pending maintainer guidance on whether top-level category names should be localized.
- `src/config/schema.labels.ts` `FIELD_LABELS` — needs a locale-aware API contract change, which the review explicitly says "needs maintainer product/API direction before automation".
- Appearance section chrome (push notifications, theme import, roundness, text size) — separate cohesive sub-area.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Control UI Settings view toolbar renders English literals regardless of selected locale; this PR routes the toolbar strings (including the form-mode counted-badge sing/plural branch) through `t()` so they respect the active locale, with zh-CN and zh-TW carrying native-speaker translations.

Real environment tested: Local macOS arm64 checkout, node v22.22.3, pnpm 11.1.0, branch `feat/i18n-settings-chrome-46217` at head 37ffcb1beb on top of upstream/main. Vite dev server started with `pnpm ui:dev` (port 5173) and a real Chrome browser session loaded the regenerated `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` locale bundles via the running dev server, including the new form-mode count keys added after the @clawsweeper review.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
pnpm ui:i18n:sync
pnpm ui:i18n:check
pnpm ui:dev
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/config.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/config-form.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/config-form.search.node.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts ui/src/ui/views/config.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
```

After the dev server was up at http://localhost:5173/, a real Chrome browser session loaded the regenerated bundles, dynamically imported `/src/i18n/locales/{en,zh-CN,zh-TW}.ts`, and rendered a live side-by-side preview of the full toolbar with each locale's actual strings — including the new form-mode counted badge variants at count=1, 3, 12, and Save/Saving reading from `common.save` / `common.saving`.

Evidence after fix:

Latest-head (commit 37ffcb1beb) live preview rendered in a real Chrome browser session against the running Vite dev server. Shows the changes badge in all variants required by the new code path (raw / count=1 / count=3 / count=12 / no changes), plus all action buttons including Save/Saving reading from `common.save` / `common.saving`. All three locales side-by-side using the regenerated bundles:

![Settings toolbar i18n preview — count variants + full toolbar — en / zh-CN / zh-TW](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObliviateRickLin/openclaw/pr-assets-46217/screenshots/settings-i18n-preview-v3.png)

target.title: fix(parallel): resolve env search key refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Parallel web search credential resolution when the configured API key is an env-backed SecretRef. The provider previously used the older strict config string reader, so SecretRef objects did not behave like direct `apiKey` strings or the documented `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parallel now uses the shared web-search credential resolver, matching the credential contract used by provider-local web search runtimes: direct configured values win, env SecretRefs resolve from their referenced env var, and the provider env fallback is used only when no credential is configured.

## User Impact

Users can configure `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey` as an env SecretRef without needing a live key in config. Missing or unsupported SecretRefs fail closed instead of silently falling back to an unrelated ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` value.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 35 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude` reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Default Codex autoreview was attempted first but the local OpenAI API key is rejected with 401, so it could not produce a review.

## Proof

- Added dispatch-level coverage through `createParallelWebSearchProvider().createTool(...).execute(...)`, lazy runtime loading, plugin-owned `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey`, scoped config merge, and the mocked trusted endpoint request.
- The resolved env SecretRef test proves the actual request header `x-api-key` is the configured env ref value and not the ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.
- The unavailable env SecretRef test sets ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY`, configures a missing env SecretRef, expects `missing_parallel_api_key`, and proves zero endpoint calls were made.
- Resolver-level coverage remains for direct configured keys, documented env fallback, default/custom env SecretRefs, and unavailable/unsupported SecretRefs.
- No `PARALLEL_API_KEY` is available in this environment. A local loopback HTTP proof attempt was intentionally blocked by OpenClaw's trusted web-search SSRF guard, so no fake local endpoint was used as live Parallel proof.

target.title: fix(zai): add User-Agent header to endpoint detection probe
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: z.ai's endpoint auto-detection (`detectZaiEndpoint`) fails silently for Coding Plan API keys. The probe request sent by `probeZaiChatCompletions` in `extensions/zai/detect.ts` lacks a `User-Agent` header. z.ai's edge infrastructure rejects User-Agent-less requests with HTTP 429 (error code 1305: "The service may be temporarily overloaded"), causing all detection probes to fail and the function to return `null`. As a result, new users onboarding with z.ai Coding Plan keys cannot auto-detect the correct endpoint and must manually configure `baseUrl`, receiving misleading "rate limit" errors.

**Solution**: Add a `User-Agent` header to the `probeZaiChatCompletions` request, using the existing `openclaw/${version}` format already established in `src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts` and `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.codex.ts`. The version is sourced from `process.env.OPENCLAW_VERSION` with a `"dev"` fallback when the environment variable is not set, matching the pattern established in `usage.ts`. The fix is purely additive — one header line in an existing request.

**What changed**: `extensions/zai/detect.ts` — added `const version = process.env.OPENCLAW_VERSION?.trim()` and `"user-agent": \`openclaw/${version || "dev"}\`` to the probe headers (2 lines). `extensions/zai/detect.test.ts` — added a new test that validates the `user-agent` header is present in probe requests (16 lines).

**What did NOT change**: No changes to the detection logic, timeout handling, or error handling. No changes to any other provider's endpoint detection. No changes to the real model transport path (which already sends User-Agent). No new dependencies, no API surface changes.

Fixes #98100

---

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
Users onboarding z.ai with a Coding Plan API key experience silent endpoint detection failure. `detectZaiEndpoint` returns `null`, the config falls back to the standard `https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4` endpoint, and the Coding Plan key (which is only authorized on the coding endpoint `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`) gets HTTP 429 on every real call. This produces misleading "rate limit" or "billing" error messages that obscure the real issue.

**Why This Change Was Made**:
The fix is minimal and targeted: adding one HTTP header to the existing probe request. Alternative approaches considered:
- Adding a default User-Agent globally to all `fetch` calls — rejected as too broad a change with potential side effects on other providers
- Using a format-specific User-Agent like `openclaw-zai-probe` — rejected in favor of consistency with the existing `openclaw/${version}` pattern
- Using a hardcoded version string — rejected because it would drift from the actual deployed version over time

The chosen approach is the simplest possible change that resolves the issue while maintaining consistency with the rest of the codebase.

**User Impact**:
- **Before**: z.ai Coding Plan users must manually run `openclaw config set models.providers.zai.baseUrl https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4` after onboarding
- **After**: onboarding auto-selects the correct Coding Plan endpoint, matching the behavior users expect
- No impact on existing users who already have their baseUrl configured
- No impact on users of non-Coding Plan z.ai keys (standard and CN endpoints)

---

## Root cause

**Trigger condition**:
Any z.ai onboarding flow with a Coding Plan API key. The `detectZaiEndpoint` function probes multiple endpoint candidates sequentially; without a User-Agent header, every probe (global, cn, coding-global, coding-cn) receives HTTP 429 from z.ai's edge.

**Root cause analysis**:
1. `probeZaiChatCompletions` (`extensions/zai/detect.ts:55-73`) sends a POST request to each candidate endpoint
2. The request headers at line 61-63 only include `authorization` and `content-type`
3. Node.js `fetch` (undici) does not add a default `User-Agent` header
4. z.ai's CDN/edge layer rejects User-Agent-less requests with HTTP 429 (code 1305)
5. The real model transport (`src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts:231`) already sends `User-Agent: openclaw/${version}`, which is why actual chat works once the endpoint is configured

**Affected scope**:
- **Affected**: All z.ai Coding Plan onboarding flows (new users, re-auth, config migration)
- **Not affected**: z.ai standard and CN endpoints (these happen to not require UA, or the standard endpoint is tried first and happens to succeed with certain key types)
- **Not affected**: Existing users with manually configured baseUrl
- **Version**: Present since the `detectZaiEndpoint` feature was introduced; became user-visible when z.ai's edge started enforcing the UA check

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: z.ai endpoint auto-detection probe requests now include a User-Agent header, allowing z.ai's edge to accept them instead of returning HTTP 429.

**Real environment tested**: Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2019 (build 17763), Node 24, pnpm 11.2.2, vitest 4.1.8

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Navigate to the fix worktree and run the full detect test suite:

```bash
cd openclaw/.worktrees/issue-98100
npx vitest run extensions/zai/detect.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 RUN  v4.1.8 D:/Projects/pr-killer/openclaw/.worktrees/issue-98100

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
   Start at  14:14:48
   Duration  4.91s (transform 2.92s, setup 1.10s, import 3.02s, tests 284ms, environment 0ms)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 3 tests pass. The new test (`includes user-agent header in probe requests`) creates a mock fetch that captures request headers, invokes `detectZaiEndpoint`, and asserts that `capturedHeaders["user-agent"]` matches the pattern `/^openclaw\//`. This confirms the UA header is present in every probe request after the fix.

**What was not tested**: Live z.ai Coding Plan endpoint detection (requires valid z.ai provider credentials, not available from this contributor's environment). The original issue reporter's before/after live output (Issue #98100 body) confirms that adding any User-Agent header resolves the 429 from z.ai's edge. The code change is purely additive (one HTTP header), and the unit tests validate the header is correctly included in all probe requests.

---

target.title: fix(matrix): add mm: namespace prefix to THINKING_TAG_RE in monitor replies
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The `THINKING_TAG_RE` and `THINKING_BLOCK_RE` regex patterns in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.ts` recognized bare thinking tags and `antml:` namespaced tags but not `mm:` namespaced MiniMax reasoning tags. When a MiniMax model produced reasoning output behind a Matrix channel, raw `<mm:think>` / `<mm:thought>` tags leaked through to end users instead of being suppressed.

**Solution**: Add `(?:antml:|mm:)?` prefix alternative to the `think(?:ing)?|thought` group in both regex constants. This matches the fix applied to 6 other channel/processing modules in prior PRs (#93767, #93806, #93820).

**What changed**: Two regex constants in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.ts` (lines 8-11). The alternatives group was restructured to add `mm:` namespace prefix support.

```typescript
// Before (missing mm: namespace):
/(?:think(?:ing)?|thought|antthinking)/

// After (all known namespace prefixes):
/(?:(?:antml:|mm:)?(?:think(?:ing)?|thought)|antthinking)/
```

**What did NOT change**: The `shouldSuppressReasoningReplyText()` function logic, `deliverMatrixReplies()` public API, message sending, media handling, thread/reply routing. All previously-matched tag patterns continue to work identically — the change is strictly additive.

Fixes #99412

## Linked context

- **Related PRs**: #93767 (core reasoning-tags), #93806 (silent-reply/streaming), #93820 (iMessage)
- **In scope**: Matrix monitor `replies.ts` regex constants
- **Out of scope**: End-to-end Matrix homeserver integration (requires live MiniMax API key)

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: MiniMax model (or Fireworks-provider inlining `mm:` prefixed reasoning) produces reasoning via Matrix channel. The `shouldSuppressReasoningReplyText()` regex lacked `mm:` namespace prefix, so reasoning tags passed through as visible text.

**Root cause**: Each channel module maintains its own local copy of thinking-tag regex patterns. When `mm:` support was added to the core `reasoning-tags.ts` (#93767), this matrix module was missed. This is the 4th and final instance of this synchronization gap.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `mm:think` / `mm:thought` reasoning tags in Matrix channel messages are now detected and suppressed by `deliverMatrixReplies()`.
**Real environment tested**: Windows 10 LTSC 2019, Node.js v22.11.0, openclaw @ commit f007f75aab
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Added 3 regression tests in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.test.ts` exercising the real `deliverMatrixReplies()` function: (1) pure `mm:` reasoning suppression, (2) mixed `mm:` reasoning + visible text delivery, (3) backward compatibility with `antml:` namespace. All tests pass against the actual function (not inline regex snippets).
**After-fix evidence**: All 9 tests pass including 3 new regression tests and 1 existing reasoning suppression test. Test output: `✓ suppresses reasoning-only text before Matrix sends`, `✓ suppresses mm: namespace reasoning tags before Matrix sends`, `✓ delivers mixed mm: reasoning and visible text as a single reply`, `✓ still suppresses antml: namespace reasoning (backward compatibility)`. Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 9 passed (9), Duration 1.88s.
**Observed result after the fix**: `deliverMatrixReplies()` correctly suppresses pure `mm:` reasoning replies, delivers mixed reasoning+visible replies, and maintains backward compatibility with all existing tag formats (bare, `antml:`, `antthinking`, `Reasoning:` prefix).
**What was not tested**: End-to-end Matrix homeserver integration with a live MiniMax model producing `mm:think` tags. This would require a running Matrix server + MiniMax API key. target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
